If we perform the resampling operation, then with uniformly positive probability (depending on M 0 , r ) we sample ˜ M = M ∗ and the points w i ∈ D W,r/ 2 such that w i ∈ B ( y i , r/ 2) for every i = 1 , . . . , M ∗ . In particular, the strands ℓ 1 i , ℓ 2 i cross the annulus A ( w i , r, 2 r ). On the event E δ the strands of Γ ∗ ,B ( w i , 2 r ) ,B ( w i ,r ) out are δ -separated. Therefore, by Corollary 3.16, the probability that ℓ 1 i , ℓ 2 i switch their linking pattern after performing the resampling is bounded from below uniformly in δ . Moreover, by continuity (Theorem 1.7) we see that with positive probability bounded from below the new strands ℓ res , 1 i , ℓ res , 2 i intersect again inside B ( w i , r/ 2). Repeating this argument M ∗ times for each target pivotal, we conclude. □

Let Γ s j ,β j be the image of Γ under ϕ j . Conditionally on G j , we have that Γ s j ,β j is a multichordal CLE κ in ( D ; s j ; β j ).

If (Γ s j ,β j ) res W,r/ 100 is F W,r/ 100 -successful, then Γ res z,j is F W z,j ,r -successful, according to Definition 5.2.
